page0.text:
"Here's your breakfast!"
Illya thrusts a plate at me as soon as I enter the living room.
Arranged on it are a black piece of toast, soft-looking sunny-side up eggs, and a neatly cut tomato.

page1.text:
"Mm. Thanks."
I accept it, still feeling dizzy, take my usual place at the dining table, and bite into the crunchy toast.
The toast aside, she did a good job on the eggs. I wonder if she learned by watching, or if Sakura or Tohsaka taught her.
Anyway, I'd better give her full marks for this first attempt.

page2.text:
"It's good."
I keep chewing on the toast.
Illya watches me eat, looking neither proud or ecstatic, just satisfied.

page3.text:
I avoid saying that the toast has the texture of charcoal. Wouldn't want to ruin the mood.
Because it actually does taste good.
Everyone has their own preferences. Some people happen to like their toast black and hard.

page4.text:
"Oh, come on. Eating burned food like that is bad for you."
"You fool. Whether it's rice or bread, it's always nice to have a dark crust."
"...Hey Emiya, did you hit your head?"
"It's good, really. It's okay to be a bit rough with cooking."
"You really must be still half-asleep... This is no time to be so carefree, you know."

page5.text:
Tohsaka looks at the TV.
It's on and playing the news.

page6.text:
Am I having deja vu?
The story they're talking about should have happened a long time ago—Suddenly, my sluggish mind kicks back into gear.

page7.text:
I read the captions on the screen:
Comas in Shinto, last night in the early dawn.
People lost consciousness and didn't wake up.
It's believed to have the same cause as the mass poisonings that happened recently, but something is different about them.
They were affected in an area 50 meters wide.
It had only happened within a single building or so before, but the radius of this latest incident was dramatically wider.

page8.text:
...But that isn't the problem.
At the end of the news report, the number of victims is listed.
Three digits' worth of people in the hospital...and people missing, too.

page9.text:
"Tohsaka, this is..."
"Yeah. Fourteen missing people. I'm sure that number will go up the more they investigate, but it looks like about a tenth of the total victims were completely consumed."

page11.text:
"Get it? I don't know if Zouken or the Shadow is behind this, but either way, the number of victims is on a whole new level.
At this rate, they might eat a whole city block in a few days."

page12.text: ...I squeeze my wrapped left arm tightly.

page13.text:
"Tohsaka. Are the people who are missing..."
Dead? I confirm with her.
Without saying anything, she looks away and nods.

page14.text:
"...Conversation's over. I know how you feel, but you can feel guilty later.
They're starting to do whatever they want in the city because they can't come directly after us. They're getting sloppy because they don't see us as a threat.
So, there's only one thing to do while they're underestimating us."
